description: Catalog of internet and cloud service types. Stable layer: it answers what each thing is, what it is for, and what units it is measured in. It contains no prices or specific providers: those live in offers.json.

families.name: Networking and delivery
families.summary: How your service reaches the people who use it.

families.name: Communication
families.summary: How your system talks to people.

families.name: Identity and security
families.summary: Who gets in and what they can do.

families.name: Development and operations
families.summary: How you build, publish, and monitor.

families.name: Artificial intelligence
families.summary: Services that interpret or generate content.

families.name: Job orchestration
families.summary: What runs, when, and in what order.

types.name: Virtual machine (VM, IaaS)
types.what_it_is: A complete computer that you rent by the hour, with its own operating system, and over which you have full control.
types.purpose: Run anything without platform restrictions, when you need to be in charge of the environment or the provider doesn't offer something more convenient.
pitfalls: You pay for it while it's on, even if nobody is using it.
Administration is on you: security patches, certificates, reboots.

types.name: Dedicated server (bare metal)
types.what_it_is: An entire physical machine just for you, with no processor shared with other customers.
types.purpose: Constant, heavy workloads, or when performance can't depend on what the neighbors are doing.
pitfalls: It's contracted by the month, not by the hour: not suited to one-off spikes.
No neighbors, but also no automatic migration if the hardware fails.

types.name: Managed containers (CaaS)
types.what_it_is: You hand over a container image and the provider runs it, scales it, and shuts it down without you administering servers.
types.purpose: Publish an application with a Dockerfile and forget about the machine, paying for actual use.
pitfalls: When it scales to zero, the first visit after a quiet spell waits for the cold start.
Free quotas are usually per account, not per service.

types.name: Serverless functions (FaaS)
types.what_it_is: You upload a standalone function and it runs when something triggers it, with no server of yours sitting there waiting.
types.purpose: Short, sporadic tasks: responding to a webhook, processing an upload, running something every hour.
pitfalls: There are hard limits on duration and request size (AWS Lambda cuts off at 6 MB per synchronous invocation).
Keeping state between calls isn't reliable: each execution may run on a different machine.

Watch out for the minimum rounding per invocation: DigitalOcean bills a minimum of 100 ms, so a function that responds in 5 ms is charged twenty times its real cost. It's worth checking this before splitting your logic into many tiny functions.

types.name: Edge compute
types.what_it_is: Your code runs in hundreds of cities at once, at the network point closest to each visitor.
types.purpose: Very fast responses worldwide without choosing a region, and lightweight work in front of a heavier system.
pitfalls: The limit is usually a PER-REQUEST CAP on CPU milliseconds, not a monthly pool: an expensive operation always fails.
It isn't full Node.js: some system APIs don't exist.

types.name: Application platform (PaaS)
types.what_it_is: You connect a repository and the platform builds, deploys, and serves the application for you.
types.purpose: Publish quickly without touching infrastructure, with automatic deployment on every code change.
pitfalls: Free plans usually suspend the application when it's inactive and take close to a minute to wake it up.
Some free plans don't allow a custom certificate on your own domain.

types.name: Managed Kubernetes
types.what_it_is: The provider maintains the brain of the cluster and you supply the machines where your containers run.
types.purpose: Coordinate many services that are deployed and scaled independently.
pitfalls: The control plane is sometimes billed separately and sometimes free: it varies by provider.
It's the option with the most operational complexity in the catalog; it's rarely justified for fewer than about ten services.

types.name: Batch jobs
types.what_it_is: Runs that start, process a volume of work, and finish, without serving requests.
types.purpose: Process files, generate reports, migrate data: long-running things nobody is waiting on at a screen.
pitfalls: Using spare capacity (spot) is much cheaper, but you can be interrupted midway.

types.name: GPUs and accelerators
types.what_it_is: Specialized cards that perform a huge number of math operations in parallel.
types.purpose: Train or run artificial intelligence models, and process video or graphics at scale.
pitfalls: It's the most expensive item in the catalog and there is almost never a free tier.
Availability is a real problem: popular models are often out of stock.

types.name: Object storage
types.what_it_is: A repository of files accessible by web address, with no real folders or file system.
types.purpose: Store things that are read a lot and modified little: images, attachments, backups, videos.
pitfalls: Storage is cheap; getting the data out is what costs (with exceptions such as Cloudflare R2, which has no egress charge).
Listing the contents counts as an expensive operation, even if you don't write anything.

types.name: Block storage (disks)
types.what_it_is: A virtual disk that attaches to a machine and behaves like a physical disk.
types.purpose: Make a machine's data survive its reboot, and give a database fast disk.
pitfalls: You keep paying for the disk even if you shut the machine down.
It attaches to only one machine at a time; to share, you need file storage.

types.name: Shared file storage
types.what_it_is: A network folder that several machines can mount and use at the same time.
types.purpose: When several servers need to read and write the same files simultaneously.
pitfalls: Quite a bit more expensive per GB than object storage.
Latency makes it a poor candidate for databases.

types.name: Cold or archive storage
types.what_it_is: Very cheap storage for data that is almost never read and takes time to retrieve.
types.purpose: Keep, out of legal or historical obligation, things you aren't going to look up.
pitfalls: There's a minimum retention period: deleting early is billed anyway.
Retrieval costs money and can take hours.
It's cheap to fill and expensive to empty.

types.name: Content delivery network (CDN)
types.what_it_is: A network of servers that keep copies of your files close to each visitor.
types.purpose: Make the web load fast in any country and have your origin server receive far less traffic.
pitfalls: If the content changes, you need to know how to invalidate the cache or stale material gets served.
Traffic pricing varies by continent.

types.name: Managed backups
types.what_it_is: A service that makes and keeps automatic copies of your disks or databases.
types.purpose: Be able to roll back after an accidental deletion, an attack, or a failure.
pitfalls: A backup that has never been restored isn't a backup: it's an assumption.
Long retention silently multiplies the cost.

types.name: Relational database (SQL)
types.what_it_is: Data organized in tables with relationships between them, queried with the SQL language.
types.purpose: Almost any application with related data: users, orders, transactions, inventories.
pitfalls: Almost no hyperscaler gives it away permanently; Azure is the notable exception.
The number of simultaneous connections runs out before the CPU does in applications without connection pooling.

types.name: Document database (NoSQL)
types.what_it_is: Stores free-form documents instead of rows with fixed columns.
types.purpose: Heterogeneous data or data that changes shape, and simple horizontal scaling.
pitfalls: There are no joins between collections: what is one query in SQL is several here.
Migrating from SQL to a document database forces you to rewrite the entire data layer, not just the queries.

types.name: Key-value store and cache
types.what_it_is: Stores key-value pairs in memory, with responses in microseconds.
types.purpose: Remember sessions, store expensive results that have already been computed, and limit the rate of requests.
pitfalls: If it's memory-only, a restart wipes everything: don't store anything there that you can't recompute.

types.name: Analytical store (data warehouse)
types.what_it_is: A database designed to scan enormous volumes of historical data and answer aggregate questions.
types.purpose: Reports, dashboards, and analysis over millions of records.
pitfalls: It is usually billed by data scanned: a poorly written query can cost a lot of money in seconds.
It's a good idea to set spending limits before letting anyone explore.

types.name: Vector database
types.what_it_is: Stores numeric representations of text or images and finds the ones most similar to each other.
types.purpose: Search by meaning and question-answering systems over your own documents.
pitfalls: It's billed by dimensions stored and queried: the size of the embeddings model determines the cost.
Many cases can be solved with ordinary text search, which is cheaper.

types.name: Time-series database
types.what_it_is: Optimized for data that arrives stamped with the time and is queried by time ranges.
types.purpose: Sensors, system metrics, stock quotes: anything that is measured repeatedly.
pitfalls: Tagging with highly varied values multiplies the number of series and the bill.

types.name: Graph database
types.what_it_is: Stores entities and the relationships between them as first-class citizens.
types.purpose: Social networks, fraud detection, recommendations: questions about paths and connections.
pitfalls: Niche: if your questions aren't about chained relationships, SQL is enough and costs less.

types.name: Distributed or edge SQL database
types.what_it_is: Managed, replicated SQLite, designed to live close to edge compute.
types.purpose: Small or medium applications that want real SQL without administering a database server.
pitfalls: It's billed by rows read, not rows returned: without indexes, a single query can drain the quota.
Some plans limit queries per invocation, not just per month.

types.name: Data transfer (egress)
types.what_it_is: The traffic that leaves the provider's infrastructure toward the internet.
types.purpose: It isn't purchased separately: it's the cost that comes along with everything else.
pitfalls: It's the most common hidden cost of the cloud.
The price varies a lot by region: sending data out of South America can cost six times more than out of the United States.
Ingress is almost always free: it's easy to put data in and expensive to take it out.

types.name: Load balancer
types.what_it_is: Spreads visits across several copies of your application and sets aside the ones that don't respond.
types.purpose: Handle more traffic and survive the failure of an instance.
pitfalls: It has a fixed hourly cost that runs even when there's no traffic.
It often ends up costing more than the small machine it serves.

types.name: Managed DNS
types.what_it_is: The service that translates your domain name to the server's address.
types.purpose: So people type your domain and arrive, and so you can move the service elsewhere without anyone noticing.
pitfalls: Changes take time to propagate, depending on the configured TTL.
It's critical infrastructure: if it goes down, everything else looks down.

types.name: Static IP address
types.what_it_is: A network address that belongs to you and doesn't change when the machine restarts.
types.purpose: When a third party needs to authorize your specific address, or to send email with a good reputation.
pitfalls: Several providers charge for the reserved IP precisely when it is NOT in use.
IPv4 addresses are a scarce resource and getting more expensive.

types.name: Virtual private cloud (VPC)
types.what_it_is: An isolated network where your services talk to each other without going over the internet.
types.purpose: So the database isn't exposed to the world and only your application can reach it.
pitfalls: It's usually free within a region and charged between regions or between zones.
It's an enormous security gain for almost no cost: you should always use it.

types.name: TLS certificates (HTTPS)
types.what_it_is: The document that encrypts the connection and proves your site is who it says it is.
types.purpose: So the padlock appears in the browser and passwords don't travel in the clear.
pitfalls: Free and automatic almost everywhere thanks to Let's Encrypt.
Some free plans do NOT allow a certificate on your own domain, only on the provider's subdomain.

types.name: Web application firewall and DDoS protection
types.what_it_is: A filter in front of your application that blocks attacks and malicious traffic.
types.purpose: Survive flooding attacks and stop automated intrusion attempts.
pitfalls: Poorly tuned rules block legitimate users.
Basic protection is usually included; advanced protection is paid for separately.

types.name: Private access without implicit trust
types.what_it_is: Publishes an internal service while requiring identity, without opening ports or setting up a traditional VPN.
types.purpose: Give access to an internal dashboard from anywhere without exposing it to the internet.
pitfalls: It's billed per person with access, so it scales with the size of the team.

types.name: API gateway
types.what_it_is: A single front door in front of your services that authenticates, rate-limits, and routes requests.
types.purpose: Expose a public API with central control over access and usage.
pitfalls: At high volume it can cost more than the compute it provides access to.

types.name: Transactional email
types.what_it_is: Automatic sending of individual emails triggered by system actions.
types.purpose: Confirmations, password recovery, notices, invoices.
pitfalls: Sending is easy; getting into the inbox is not. You have to configure SPF, DKIM, and DMARC.
VPS providers usually block port 25 to curb spam.

types.name: Mailboxes
types.what_it_is: Email accounts on your domain that people read and write.
types.purpose: The team's email: hello@yourdomain.com.
pitfalls: It's billed per mailbox per month; aliases are usually free and often enough.

types.name: SMS and messaging
types.what_it_is: Sending text messages or messaging-app messages from your system.
types.purpose: Verification codes, urgent alerts, reminders.
pitfalls: The price varies enormously by country: never estimate with a single rate.
Many countries require you to register the sender before allowing messages to be sent.

types.name: Push notifications
types.what_it_is: Alerts that appear on the phone or in the browser even when the application is closed.
types.purpose: Win back someone's attention at no per-message cost.
pitfalls: It's usually free or nearly so, but it requires explicit permission and is easily revoked if you abuse it.

types.name: Voice and telephony (VoIP)
types.what_it_is: Making and receiving phone calls from software.
types.purpose: Phone switchboards (PBX), call-based alerts, voice verification.
pitfalls: You pay for the number per month in addition to the minutes.
Quality depends on the user's network, not just the provider.

types.name: Real-time video
types.what_it_is: Infrastructure for live video and audio calls among several people.
types.purpose: Video calls, virtual classrooms, remote support.
pitfalls: It's billed per minute and per person: the cost grows quickly with group size.
Recording and storing are billed separately.

types.name: Real-time messaging
types.what_it_is: A permanent channel between server and browser for sending changes instantly.
types.purpose: Chats, collaborative boards, live scores, instant notifications.
pitfalls: It's billed by simultaneous connections: a hundred people watching costs a hundred connections even if nobody writes.

types.name: Message queues
types.what_it_is: A to-do list of pending tasks that one service drops off and another picks up when it can.
types.purpose: Decouple slow processes from the response to the user and absorb work spikes.
pitfalls: Putting messages in and taking them out are counted separately.
You need a dead-letter queue or errors get retried forever.

types.name: Webhooks and event bus
types.what_it_is: Automatic notices that one system sends to another when something happens.
types.purpose: So that a confirmed payment triggers an email, or a change in one tool updates another.
pitfalls: You have to verify the signature or anyone can fake the notice.
They get resent: the receiver must tolerate receiving the same thing twice (idempotency).

types.name: Managed authentication
types.what_it_is: Delegating sign-up, login, and password management to a third party.
types.purpose: So you don't have to build or maintain the most sensitive system in the application yourself.
pitfalls: The price per active user scales with your success, not with your technical usage.
Switching providers is hard: the passwords are encrypted in their format.
For a handful of administrators it can be absurdly expensive compared with a login of your own.

types.name: Secrets management
types.what_it_is: An encrypted store for passwords, API keys, and certificates.
types.purpose: So credentials don't live in the code or in the repository.
pitfalls: Dedicated services are billed per secret and per retrieval; the platform's environment variables are usually enough and free.
Changing a secret almost always requires redeploying.

types.name: Encryption key management (KMS)
types.what_it_is: Safeguards cryptographic keys and performs the encryption without the key ever leaving.
types.purpose: Meet regulatory requirements and protect sensitive data at rest.
pitfalls: It's billed per key per month plus per operation: encrypting field by field makes the cost skyrocket.

types.name: Internal certificates (PKI)
types.what_it_is: Issuing your own certificates so your services authenticate each other.
types.purpose: Encrypted and verified communication inside the infrastructure.
pitfalls: An expired internal certificate takes down the entire system and usually catches people by surprise.

types.name: Auditing and compliance
types.what_it_is: A tamper-proof record of who did what in the infrastructure.
types.purpose: Investigate incidents and meet regulatory requirements.
pitfalls: The first tier is usually free; keeping a long history is billed.

types.name: Code repository
types.what_it_is: Where the code lives, along with its full change history.
types.purpose: Work as a team, review changes, and be able to go back to any point in the past.
pitfalls: Private repositories are almost always free; what gets billed is automation minutes and storage of large files.

types.name: Continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD)
types.what_it_is: Automates testing, building, and publishing every code change.
types.purpose: So that publishing stops being an error-prone manual ritual.
pitfalls: It's billed by build minutes, and macOS runners cost up to ten times more than Linux ones.
Without a dependency cache, every run pays for the entire download.

types.name: Container registry
types.what_it_is: The store where container images ready to deploy are kept.
types.purpose: So the deployment platform can download the exact version you want to publish.
pitfalls: Old images pile up and nobody deletes them: a retention policy is a good idea.
Pulling from another cloud pays egress.

types.name: Logs
types.what_it_is: The collection and search of everything your application writes down.
types.purpose: Understand what happened when something fails.
pitfalls: You pay twice: for ingesting and for retaining.
It's the line item that shoots up most without warning; it's better to log less and better.

types.name: Metrics
types.what_it_is: Numbers measured repeatedly over time: CPU usage, requests per minute, errors.
types.purpose: See trends and get alerts before users complain.
pitfalls: Tagging with unique identifiers causes a cardinality explosion and multiplies the cost.

types.name: Distributed traces
types.what_it_is: Follows the complete path of a request through all the services it touches.
types.purpose: Find where time is lost in a system with many parts.
pitfalls: Sampling is usually applied (keeping only a fraction) because storing everything is extremely expensive.

types.name: Uptime monitoring
types.what_it_is: An external robot that periodically checks whether your site responds.
types.purpose: Find out about an outage before your users do.
pitfalls: The interval determines the cost and also how long it takes you to find out.
Checking from a single region doesn't detect regional problems.

types.name: Error tracking
types.what_it_is: Collects the application's exceptions, groups them, and alerts you.
types.purpose: Know what breaks, how many people it affects, and which version it started with.
pitfalls: It's billed per event: an error in a loop can use up the month's quota in an afternoon.

types.name: Static site hosting
types.what_it_is: Publishing already-generated files (HTML, images) with no program running behind them.
types.purpose: Informational websites, documentation, portfolios, and blogs.
pitfalls: It's the most common free tier in the industry, precisely because it costs very little to serve.
It doesn't work if you need to store data or authenticate users.

types.name: Traditional shared hosting
types.what_it_is: Space on a shared server with a control panel, designed for websites using PHP and MySQL.
types.purpose: WordPress and sites run by non-technical people.
pitfalls: The “unlimited” promises are limited by the fine print.
Renewal prices usually double or triple the sign-up price.

types.name: Domain registration
types.what_it_is: The annual rental of a name on the internet.
types.purpose: Have your own stable address, independent of where you host.
pitfalls: A cheap first year and an expensive renewal is the norm; always compare the renewal price.
Make sure registration privacy (WHOIS) is included and not billed separately.

types.name: Managed search
types.what_it_is: An engine that indexes your content and answers searches with typo tolerance and relevance ranking.
types.purpose: Search for catalogs, documentation, or any large body of content.
pitfalls: It's billed per search and per indexed record.
For small catalogs, PostgreSQL or SQLite full-text search is usually enough.

types.name: Image and video processing
types.what_it_is: Resizes, crops, optimizes, and converts media on demand.
types.purpose: Serve each device the image in the right size and format without generating them by hand.
pitfalls: It's billed per unique transformation: many variants per image multiply the cost.
Video is billed per encoded minute and is an order of magnitude more expensive.

types.name: Maps and geolocation
types.what_it_is: Interactive maps, converting addresses to coordinates, and calculating routes.
types.purpose: Show locations, calculate distances, and sequence deliveries.
pitfalls: It's billed per map load and per call: a page that reloads the map burns through the quota quickly.
OpenStreetMap is a free alternative with attribution requirements.

types.name: Web analytics
types.what_it_is: Measures visits, user journeys, and conversions on your site.
types.purpose: Know what works and what doesn't, and where people come from.
pitfalls: Free options are usually paid for with your visitors' data.
In Europe there are legal implications depending on where the data is processed.

types.name: Payment gateway
types.what_it_is: Processes card or other payments and transfers the money to you.
types.purpose: Sell or receive contributions without handling card data yourself.
pitfalls: The fixed fee makes very small charges unviable: on 1 USD, a third can go to fees.
Availability by country is a decisive factor; some gateways don't operate throughout Latin America.
Handling cards on your own means PCI DSS compliance: it almost always makes sense to delegate it.

types.name: Language model (LLM)
types.what_it_is: A model that receives text and generates text, accessible via API.
types.purpose: Write, summarize, classify, extract data, and hold conversations.
pitfalls: Output costs quite a bit more than input: always separate the two when estimating.
Resending the entire history on every turn multiplies the cost of a long conversation.
Context caching can cut the bill a lot if used well.

types.name: OCR and document understanding
types.what_it_is: Extracts text—and sometimes structure—from images and PDFs.
types.purpose: Digitize receipts, invoices, and paper forms.
pitfalls: Simple OCR and structured extraction are priced very differently: there can be a tenfold difference.
Self-hosted Tesseract is free and is usually enough if the images are clean; it's worth measuring accuracy before you pay.

types.name: Speech-to-text transcription
types.what_it_is: Converts spoken audio into written text.
types.purpose: Subtitles, meeting minutes, search within recordings.
pitfalls: Accuracy drops sharply with noise, strong accents, or several people talking at once.
Speaker identification is usually billed separately.

types.name: Text-to-speech
types.what_it_is: Converts written text into spoken audio.
types.purpose: Accessibility, voice alerts, automatic narration.
pitfalls: Neural voices cost several times more than basic ones.
Cloning a voice has legal and consent implications.

types.name: Machine translation
types.what_it_is: Translates text between languages automatically.
types.purpose: Publish content in several languages without a translation team.
pitfalls: It's billed per source character, including spaces and HTML tags if you don't exclude them.

types.name: Computer vision
types.what_it_is: Analyzes images to detect objects, text, faces, or inappropriate content.
types.purpose: Moderate user-uploaded content, tag catalogs, read license plates.
pitfalls: Facial recognition is regulated or banned in several jurisdictions.

types.name: Scheduled tasks (cron)
types.what_it_is: Runs something automatically at a fixed time or interval.
types.purpose: Daily reports, periodic cleanups, reminders, syncs.
pitfalls: Almost always in UTC: local times and clock changes cause surprises.
If one run overlaps the previous one, it can duplicate work.

types.name: Workflows
types.what_it_is: Coordinates several steps with waits, retries, and state that survives failures.
types.purpose: Long processes with several stages that can't be lost halfway through.
pitfalls: It's billed per state transition: a workflow with many small steps gets expensive.

types.name: Data pipelines (ETL)
types.what_it_is: Moves data between systems, transforming it along the way.
types.purpose: Feed an analytics warehouse from production databases.
pitfalls: Managed tools charge per connector and per synced row: the cost grows with the volume of data, not with its value.
